questions.q: What does nn.Embedding do with token ID i?
choices: Multiplies i by the embedding width
Selects row i of a learnable floating-point table
questions.why: The integer is a row address. The selected floating values are the trainable parameters, not the ID.

questions.q: The lab table has shape (6, 4). Input IDs have shape (2, 3). What is the output shape?
questions.why: Embedding appends its width to the input shape: batch, token position, vector coordinate. The table still has 24 parameters.

questions.q: For nonzero u and v, what happens to cosine(u, v) when v is multiplied by a positive constant?
questions.why: The positive scale factor cancels between the dot product and the norm in the denominator. Direction is unchanged.

questions.q: Every random nonzero row has self-cosine close to one. What does this establish?
choices: The nearest neighbor search is accurate
The geometry calculation is consistent, not that learning occurred
questions.why: Self-cosine follows from a nonzero vector's geometry even before training. A training claim needs an objective and appropriate evidence.

questions.q: After the lab fits its hand-authored context targets, cat and dog have cosine 0.987241. Which claim is supported?
choices: The code discovered English semantics without supervision
Gradient descent fitted the supplied targets and their designed geometry
Any two synonyms in any model have this score
The model passes a held-out language benchmark
questions.why: These targets are a deliberately engineered fixture. The experiment proves lookup-table learning, not broad generalization or a production retrieval threshold.

questions.q: Part 3 sums table([0, 0, 1]). Predict the gradient on each coordinate of rows 0, 1, and all other rows.
questions.answer: Row 0: 2.0 per coordinate. Row 1: 1.0 per coordinate. All remaining rows: 0.0 from this loss.
questions.why: Each selected occurrence contributes one derivative to the sum. Repeated uses of the same parameter accumulate. This excludes other gradient paths and optimizer effects.

questions.q: Set the fixture training step count to zero. Will the self-cosine check or the target-convergence check fail? Explain without assuming random neighbors are sensible.
questions.answer: Self-cosine still passes for nonzero rows. Target convergence fails: the table remains at its random initialization rather than the supplied targets.
questions.why: A geometric identity is true independently of learning. A genuine fitting check compares learned weights with the required targets.

questions.q: Explain how to relabel every token ID without changing the vectors selected, and why changing only the IDs breaks the model-table contract.
rubric: IDs are addresses rather than quantities or meanings
A row permutation must be matched by an inverse mapping from old IDs to new positions
The same tokens then select the same floating vectors
Changing only one side selects the wrong rows even if shapes still look valid

questions.q: Explain why a static token table and an embedding model for document retrieval are not interchangeable.
rubric: A static lookup returns the same row for the same ID at fixed weights
A contextual model can combine surrounding tokens and position information
A document or sentence encoder produces a representation of the text rather than an arbitrary single token
Equal vector widths do not imply compatible coordinate systems or quality
Similarity does not establish source truth or authority

questions.q: New case: change dog's context counts to match run's counts. Predict the direction of the resulting geometry change and explain what has and has not been learned.
rubric: Training moves dog's vector toward its changed normalized target
Dog should now approach run's target rather than the original cat-like target
The objective follows supplied supervision, not an innate dictionary meaning of dog
A changed nearest-neighbor pattern is evidence about this fitting experiment, not general language understanding
Original fixture-specific assertions may fail appropriately and should not simply be weakened

recall.q: What is an embedding lookup, in one sentence?
recall.a: Use a discrete ID to select a learnable floating-point row; the ID is an address, not a semantic measurement.

recall.q: Why does repeated use of one token matter to backpropagation?
recall.a: Occurrences share the same row, so their gradient contributions accumulate into the same parameters.

recall.q: What does cosine ignore, and where is it mathematically undefined?
recall.a: It ignores positive rescaling of nonzero vectors. A zero vector has no direction, so its mathematical cosine is undefined; libraries may impose a numerical convention.

recall.q: Does self-cosine one prove a table learned language?
recall.a: No. It is already true for nonzero random rows. Learning needs an objective and task-appropriate evidence.

recall.q: What is the limitation of this chapter's training experiment?
recall.a: It fits explicit hand-authored context targets. It demonstrates gradient-based lookup learning but does not evaluate generalization on natural language.
